Q: Are files in the temporary folder automatically deleted? A:

Starting with Windows 10, the answer is possibly yes - depending on the machine configuration and the amount of free space on the drive hosting the TEMP folder.

Specifically, Storage Sense can arbitrarily delete files from the TEMP folder (I found that out the hard way) if enabled by the user. And from what I can tell, it will self-enable on low disk space.

Q: Print/log the names and values of all parameters a function was called with (without eval) A:

I was just wondering the same and found the wonderful function locals().

From https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#locals:

Return a mapping object representing the current local symbol table, with variable names as the keys, and their currently bound references as the values.

So my solution is just to print the locals() at the beginning of the function, which would only be the arguments of the function.

So here is a small exmaple:

import logging

# Set up some configuration for logging
FORMAT = "%(levelname)s:%(name)s [%(funcName)15s(): %(lineno)4s]: %(message)s"
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, stream=sys.stdout, format=FORMAT)


def my_function(a=None, lot=None, of=None, arguments=None):
    logging.debug("params %s", locals())
    # do some stuff
    print("This is what my function does.")

my_function()

This prints:

DEBUG:root [    my_function():    2]: params {'a': None, 'lot': None, 'of': None, 'arguments': None}

This is what my function does.

Q: Is it possible to run TrueNAS on a docker? A:

No, since it makes totally no sense to put TrueNAS inside of Docker. TrueNAS is more an OS than a service; it needs direct access to the disks that it manages and provides services like NFS, SMB, and iSCSI. The better way is to install TrueNAS on the machine and let it run Docker containers inside (it has this functionality out of the box).

When you only want to play around with TrueNAS, put it in a Virtual Machine (KVM) on your Debian installation and give it some "qcow2" disks to play around with, but you will not get any good performance out of this. If you have additional disks, sure, you can give them from the host "raw" to the TrueNAS guest.

But these are all not production setups—maybe for homelabs to play around with technology.

Q: Application won't end after pressing the x on the second window A:

There are few issues in your code:

  • multiple instances of CTk
  • create child window newPlace with hidden parent master, use window instead
  • create button FinalEnd with hidden parent master, use newPlace instead
  • typo destory, should be destroy instead
  • anchor="SE" should be anchor="se" instead

Updated code to fix the above issues:

import customtkinter as ctk

#master = ctk.CTk() # don't need
def open_window_button():
    newPlace = ctk.CTkToplevel(window)  # use window as parent
    newPlace.title("peneer")
    newPlace.geometry("400x150")

    FinalEnd = ctk.CTkButton(newPlace, anchor="se", command=window.destroy) # use newPlace as parent and fix typo
    FinalEnd.pack(padx=20, pady=20)



ctk.set_appearance_mode("dark")

window = ctk.CTk()
window.title("My Life")
window.geometry("400x150")

button = ctk.CTkButton(window,anchor="center", text="Press me ;)", fg_color='#0e6b0e', hover_color='#149414', command=open_window_button, text_color="black")
button.pack(expand=True,padx=20, pady=20)

window.mainloop()
